rationale: This is just a rank-sum of two long-documented standalone anomalies — the R&D-to-assets effect and the external-financing/composite-issuance effect — so any measured spread will almost surely be the additive combination of known premia rather than a genuine interaction.

The multiplicative conditioning of R&D capital on net repurchase is a defensible "insider-validated intangibles" interaction with a coherent sign, but both legs (Peters–Taylor style knowledge capital, net payout/net share issuance) are individually famous, so the burden is on the interaction to deliver alpha beyond the double-sort baseline.

Stock-financed acquirer underperformance is one of the most heavily documented anomalies in the literature (Loughran–Vijh, Rau–Vermaelen, plus the goodwill/asset-growth overlap), so this is a direct rediscovery rather than a novel cross-theme signal.

The expected positive loading on net long-term debt issuance runs against the well-established evidence that *all* forms of external financing (debt included) predict low returns, so the debt-monitoring story needs justification before the composite is worth testing; the R&D-intensity gate is also a rank in [0,1] that shrinks rather than switches, leaving non-innovators clustered at zero in the middle of the cross-section.

This is structurally the same rank-difference as "Self-Funded Innovation Gap" with csho growth substituted for dollar issuance — i.e., a cosmetic variant whose short leg is the canonical net share issuance anomaly — and the ACCEL second difference of R&D/at is likely too noisy to contribute independent signal.

Conditioning external financing on a multi-year decline in revenue per unit of intangible capital is a genuinely non-obvious productivity-gated version of the issuance effect with internally consistent sign and construction; watch coverage and denominator instability, since `intan` is missing or near zero for many firms and the 5-year TREND requirement will thin the sample.
